info.short_name: Sex
info.long_name: Evaluated sex
info.short_description: Evaluated sex recorded at the emergency department encounter.
info.long_description: Evaluated sex as recorded in the Epic Cosmos ED Encounters data model. 'Male' and 'Female' are the recorded sexes, 'Ambiguous' is Epic's category for encounters whose evaluated sex is recorded as ambiguous, and 'Overall' is the total across all evaluated sex categories, including encounters with no evaluated sex recorded, which are not published as their own stratum. The 'Ambiguous' stratum is small and heavily suppressed, and its derived epic_ed_pct_visits_* values are the noisiest in the file because they rest on percentages near the two-decimal reporting floor. Read it with care.

info.short_name: Average ED length of stay: Suicidal behavior
info.long_name: Average emergency department length of stay for Suicidal behavior encounters
info.short_description: Average time in minutes from ED arrival to ED departure for Suicidal behavior encounters.
info.long_description: Mean emergency department length of stay in minutes for Suicidal behavior. Encounters are Epic Cosmos ED encounters with a United States country of residence, attributed to the patient's state of residence and to the calendar month of arrival, and assigned to the Suicidal behavior bucket of the ED Diagnoses grouper. Length of stay runs from arrival to ED departure, so it includes boarding time for patients awaiting an inpatient or psychiatric bed. The mean is computed by Epic Cosmos over the encounters in each cell and is right-skewed by long boarders, so it sits above the typical stay - compare it with epic_ed_los_median_suicidal_behavior to gauge the skew. A small number of averages are negative in the source (four cells, from encounters whose recorded departure precedes arrival). They cannot be real elapsed times but are retained as published; filter on value >= 0 if a non-negative duration is required. Cells built on 10 or fewer encounters are suppressed at source and left missing; a missing value and a suppression flag of 1 mean exactly the same thing, because every value the source published is carried through as published. Note that the 'All ED encounters' variant is the total row of the ED Diagnoses grouper: it covers every ED encounter, including the non-mental-health diagnoses not displayed as their own columns, and is not a total of the mental health buckets.

info.short_name: Suppressed flag: average ED length of stay, Suicidal behavior
info.long_name: Suppression flag for the Suicidal behavior average ED length of stay
info.short_description: Indicates whether the Suicidal behavior average ED length of stay was suppressed at source.
info.long_description: This flag is 1 when Epic Cosmos suppressed the Suicidal behavior average ED length of stay because the cell was built on 10 or fewer encounters, and 0 otherwise. These statistics are not counts, so a suppressed value cannot be imputed - there is no published denominator to impute a numerator against - and epic_ed_los_avg_suicidal_behavior is left missing wherever this flag is 1. Nothing is dropped during ingestion, so a flag of 1 and a missing value coincide exactly: the flag is equivalent to is.na() on the measure, and is provided so the reason for the gap is explicit. Check it before comparing across geographies: suppression is heavy in the sparser diagnosis buckets, reaching roughly four in five cells for eating disorders.

info.short_description: Median time in minutes from ED arrival to ED departure for Eating disorders encounters.
info.long_description: Median emergency department length of stay in minutes for Eating disorders. Encounters are Epic Cosmos ED encounters with a United States country of residence, attributed to the patient's state of residence and to the calendar month of arrival, and assigned to the Eating disorders bucket of the ED Diagnoses grouper. Length of stay runs from arrival to ED departure, so it includes boarding time for patients awaiting an inpatient or psychiatric bed. This is the most robust of the length-of-stay statistics in this source: unlike the mean, standard deviation, minimum and maximum, it is not distorted by the small number of encounters with corrupted arrival or departure timestamps, and it is the recommended default for trend and cross-state comparison. It runs well below the mean for every mental health bucket, which is the signature of a long right tail of boarded patients. Cells built on 10 or fewer encounters are suppressed at source and left missing; a missing value and a suppression flag of 1 mean exactly the same thing, because every value the source published is carried through as published. Note that the 'All ED encounters' variant is the total row of the ED Diagnoses grouper: it covers every ED encounter, including the non-mental-health diagnoses not displayed as their own columns, and is not a total of the mental health buckets.

epic_ed_pct_visits_suicidal_behavior.short_name: Percent of ED encounters: Suicidal behavior
epic_ed_pct_visits_suicidal_behavior.long_name: Percentage of emergency department encounters with a Suicidal behavior diagnosis
epic_ed_pct_visits_suicidal_behavior.short_description: Percent of all ED encounters in the geography, month and sex stratum that carried a Suicidal behavior diagnosis.
epic_ed_pct_visits_suicidal_behavior.long_description: Share of emergency department encounters accounted for by Suicidal behavior, as a percentage of all ED encounters in the same geography, month and sex stratum. Encounters are Epic Cosmos ED encounters with a United States country of residence, attributed to the patient's state of residence and to the calendar month of arrival, and assigned to the Suicidal behavior bucket of the ED Diagnoses grouper. DERIVED MEASURE. The source publishes a 'Percentage of Sliced Population' field whose denominator depends on the cell's position in the crosstab: within a sex group it is that sex's share of the geography's encounters for the diagnosis, on the all-sex row it is the geography's share of national encounters for the diagnosis, and on the national all-sex row it is the diagnosis's share of all encounters. Those are three different quantities, so the raw field is not publishable as a single column. This column rescales them onto one definition, using the national diagnosis mix and each geography's all-cause share as the bridge. Two independent checks support it: the national mix read directly off the export matches the median of the separately derived state shares, and the seven mental health buckets together account for a median 6.1% of ED encounters (IQR 5.2-7.5%), consistent with published estimates of the mental health share of ED volume. Two caveats. The source percentages are rounded to two decimal places, so for rare buckets - eating disorders in particular, which sits at the 0.01% reporting floor nationally - the derived share carries substantial relative rounding error. And the diagnosis buckets are not guaranteed to be mutually exclusive, so the buckets should not be assumed to sum exactly to a total. The all-cause variant is omitted: it is 100% by construction. Missing where any input percentage was suppressed at source.

epic_cosmos.name: Epic Cosmos
epic_cosmos.description: Epic Cosmos is a collaborative research platform containing de-identified patient data from over 300 million patients across more than 1,600 hospitals and health systems using Epic electronic health record systems. Data is accessed via SlicerDicer, a self-service analytics tool. The dataset includes emergency department visits, diagnoses, immunizations, laboratory results, and other clinical data. Due to privacy protections, counts fewer than 10 are suppressed and imputed. Coverage extends across all U.S. states and territories. Note that county-level and city-level stratifications could differ markedly in total sample size due to high levels of missingness of county data in some states.
epic_cosmos.restrictions: The data can be re-used with appropriate attribution. A suggested citation relating to this data is 'Results of research performed with Epic Cosmos were obtained from the PopHIVE platform (https://github.com/PopHIVE/Ingest).'
